claim.text: Normal GNU Prolog startup forces C numeric locale even when environment selects a comma-decimal locale; separately, source literals may or may not be invariant to a post-start locale mutation
claim.scope: Eight decimal literals, compiled/consulted mode, ELF64 and i686 ELF32, C/de_DE.UTF-8 environments
assumptions: GNU Prolog Pl_Start_Prolog invokes Set_Locale at process startup
de_DE.UTF-8 exists and has comma decimal point in CI
The test-only forced mutation executes strictly after Set_Locale
forbidden_promotions: No assertion that setting LC_ALL alone causes misparse
Do not conflate startup normalization with foreign postinit mutation resilience
No independent physical 32-bit or external-reproduction claim

specification.intended_object: Two typed claims: normal startup normalization, and post-initialization mutation resilience
invariants: C and de environment without mutation both use effective LC_NUMERIC=C at sscanf
All eight normal-mode literals match independent exact-rational binary64 bits
Forced mutation actually yields comma numeric locale
Any value mismatch under forced mutation explicitly falsifies its separate invariance claim

preregistration.primary_metric: Any ordinary startup value mismatch or failure to normalize LC_NUMERIC=C
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Deterministic per-fixture C observations; no statistical confidence interval
preregistration.kill_condition: Normal startup value mismatch, missing trace, wrong locale state or crash kills primary claim; forced differing bits kill separate mutation-resilience claim

preregistration.promotion_rule: M for separately supported startup claim, R for any falsified post-init invariance; never promote both from a single green CI
